title: Reported speech II: she said, she claimed, she asked me to
title_target: Hon bad mig att säga till om jag fastnade.
goal: Retell a conversation in Swedish: shift the tenses back, choose the right reporting verb, and report questions and requests with *frågade om* and *bad mig att*.
bekal: you can shift tenses in reported speech (*är → var*, *har sett → hade sett*, *ska → skulle*)
you can use reporting verbs beyond *sa*: *påstå, berätta, förklara, lova, erkänna*
you can report questions (*hon undrade om…*) and requests (*hon bad mig att…*)
wave: Go back to Unit 11: take the indirect questions you made there (*Jag vet inte vem som ringde*) and put them in the past — *Hon undrade vem som hade ringt* — keeping *som* where the question word is the subject.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Halvtidssamtalet
dialogs.intro: Dian is halfway through her internship, and Karin has booked a half-hour check-in with her in the small meeting room on the third floor.

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Nu har du varit här i tre månader. Hur känns det?
lines.id: You've been here three months now. How does it feel?
lines.literal: now have you been here in three months. how feels it?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Jättebra. Jag lär mig mycket, men ibland är jag osäker på min svenska.
lines.id: Really good. I'm learning a lot, but sometimes I'm unsure about my Swedish.
lines.literal: giant-good. I learn myself much, but sometimes am I unsure on my Swedish.

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Det märks inte. Kunden sa faktiskt att din presentation var den bästa.
lines.id: It doesn't show. The client actually said your presentation was the best one.
lines.literal: it notice-s not. client-the said actually that your presentation was the best.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Sa hon verkligen det? Jag trodde att hon tyckte att jag pratade för fort.
lines.id: Did she really say that? I thought she felt I talked too fast.
lines.literal: said she really that? I thought that she thought that I talked too fast.

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Nej, hon påstod att du var lättare att förstå än vi andra!
lines.id: No, she claimed you were easier to understand than the rest of us!
lines.literal: no, she claimed that you were easier to understand than we others!

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Vad roligt att höra. Får jag fråga en sak? Kan jag vara med på fler kundmöten?
lines.id: That's so nice to hear. Can I ask something? Could I join more client meetings?
lines.literal: what fun to hear. may I ask a thing? can I be with on more client-meetings?

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Absolut. Och jag vill att du tar hand om nästa projekt själv, med Mattias som stöd.
lines.id: Absolutely. And I want you to run the next project yourself, with Mattias as support.
lines.literal: absolutely. and I want that you take hand about next project self, with Mattias as support.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Själv? Är du säker på att jag klarar det?
lines.id: By myself? Are you sure I can manage it?
lines.literal: self? are you sure on that I manage it?

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Helt säker. Men lova mig en sak: säg till om du fastnar.
lines.id: Completely sure. But promise me one thing: tell me if you get stuck.
lines.literal: wholly sure. but promise me a thing: say to if you get-stuck.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Jag lovar. Och tack för att du tror på mig.
lines.id: I promise. And thank you for believing in me.
lines.literal: I promise. and thanks for that you believe on me.

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Det gör jag. Förresten, kommer du att stanna i Göteborg efter praktiken?
lines.id: I do. By the way, are you going to stay in Göteborg after the internship?
lines.literal: that do I. by-the-way, come you to stay in Göteborg after internship-the?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Det vet jag inte än. Jag måste tänka på det.
lines.id: I don't know yet. I have to think about it.
lines.literal: that know I not yet. I must think on it.

notes: **Hur känns det? — Det märks inte.** — two more *-s* verbs: *kännas* (**SHEN-nahs**, to feel — about a situation, not a person: *det känns bra*) and *märkas* (**MEHR-kahs**, to show, to be noticeable). *Det märks att du har bott i Göteborg* — You can tell you've lived in Göteborg.

**Kunden sa att din presentation var den bästa** — the client's actual words were *Hennes presentation **är** den bästa*. Reported after a past verb (*sa*), the present shifts back to the past: *…att din presentation **var** den bästa*. Swedish follows the same rule as English here, so trust your instinct.

**hon påstod att…** — *påstå* (**POH-stoh**: *påstår – påstod – har påstått*) means "to claim". Like English "claim", it can hint that the speaker isn't sure it's true. Karin uses it jokingly — she's teasing herself and Mattias.

**jag vill att du tar hand om…** — "I want you to…" can't be copied word for word into Swedish: *jag vill dig att…* is impossible. Use **vill att** + a full clause: *Jag vill att du kommer*, *Vill du att jag hjälper dig?*

**säg till om du fastnar** — *säga till* (**seh-yah TIL**, stress on the particle) means "to let someone know, to speak up": *Säg till om du behöver något!* (Just say if you need anything!). *Fastna* (**FAHST-nah**) is "to get stuck" — in a task, in traffic, or literally in a door.

**tack för att du tror på mig** — *tro på* means "to believe in" (a person, an idea). After *tack för att*, Swedish uses a full clause where English uses "-ing": *tack för att du kom* (thanks for coming).

grammars.title: Tense shift in reported speech
body: When the reporting verb is in the past (*sa, berättade, förklarade, påstod*), each verb in the reported clause usually moves one step back in time.

head: Direct speech
Reported speech
Example
rows: "Jag är trött." → Hon sa att hon **var** trött.
"Jag var sjuk." → Han sa att han **hade varit** sjuk.
"Jag har sett filmen." → Han sa att han **hade sett** filmen.
"Jag ska ringa." → Hon lovade att hon **skulle** ringa.
"Jag kan inte." → Hon sa att hon inte **kunde**.

after: If something is **still true**, you may keep the present: *Hon sa att Göteborg **är** vackert.* In relaxed speech many Swedes skip the shift entirely when it's obvious. In writing, shift.

Words for *here* and *now* also move when the time and place have changed: *här → där*, *nu → då*, *i dag → den dagen*, *i går → dagen innan*, *i morgon → dagen efter*. And pronouns change with the speaker: *"jag"* becomes *hon*, *"min"* becomes *hennes*: *"Min chef är nöjd"* → *Hon sa att **hennes** chef var nöjd*. (*Sin* is impossible here, because *hennes chef* is the subject of its own clause — see Unit 8.)
Remember BIFF: the reported clause is a subordinate clause, so *inte* jumps ahead of the verb — *Hon sa att hon **inte kunde**.*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Dian ringer Elin
dialogs.intro: That evening Dian calls Elin in Stockholm. Elin has been waiting all day to hear how the meeting went.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Hej! Hur gick samtalet med chefen?
lines.id: Hi! How did the talk with your boss go?
lines.literal: hi! how went conversation-the with boss-the?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Över förväntan! Karin sa att kunden hade varit jättenöjd med min presentation.
lines.id: Better than expected! Karin said the client had been really happy with my presentation.
lines.literal: over expectation! Karin said that client-the had been giant-satisfied with my presentation.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Vad sa jag? Jag sa ju att du skulle klara det.
lines.id: What did I tell you? I told you you'd manage it.
lines.literal: what said I? I said ju that you would manage it.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Och kunden påstod tydligen att jag var lättare att förstå än de andra.
lines.id: And apparently the client claimed I was easier to understand than the others.
lines.literal: and client-the claimed apparently that I was easier to understand than the others.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Ha! Det berättar vi inte för Mattias. Vad mer sa Karin?
lines.id: Ha! We won't tell Mattias that. What else did Karin say?
lines.literal: ha! that tell we not for Mattias. what more said Karin?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Hon förklarade att jag skulle få ett eget projekt, och hon bad mig att säga till om jag fastnade.
lines.id: She explained that I'd get a project of my own, and she asked me to let her know if I got stuck.
lines.literal: she explained that I would get an own project, and she asked me to say to if I got-stuck.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Ett eget projekt! Frågade hon om du ville stanna i Göteborg också?
lines.id: A project of your own! Did she ask whether you wanted to stay in Göteborg, too?
lines.literal: an own project! asked she if you wanted stay in Göteborg also?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ja, hon undrade om jag skulle stanna efter praktiken. Jag sa att jag inte visste än.
lines.id: Yes, she wondered if I'd be staying after the internship. I said I didn't know yet.
lines.literal: yes, she wondered if I would stay after internship-the. I said that I not knew yet.

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Lova mig att du inte bestämmer något utan att prata med mig först.
lines.id: Promise me you won't decide anything without talking to me first.
lines.literal: promise me that you not decide anything without to talk with me first.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Jag lovar. Det var ju du som sa att jag skulle våga mer!
lines.id: I promise. You were the one who said I should be braver!
lines.literal: I promise. it was ju you who said that I should dare more!

lines.speaker: Elin:
lines.text: Det sa jag. Men jag menade inte att du skulle flytta till Göteborg för alltid!
lines.id: I did say that. But I didn't mean you should move to Göteborg forever!
lines.literal: that said I. but I meant not that you should move to Göteborg for ever!

notes: **kunden hade varit jättenöjd** — here the shift goes two steps back. The client's own words were *Jag **är** nöjd* (present); by the time Karin reported them, they had become *hon **var** nöjd*; and now Dian reports Karin's report: *…att kunden **hade varit** nöjd*. The pluperfect marks "further back than the moment of reporting".

**Jag sa ju att du skulle klara det** — *ska* (or *kommer att*) becomes **skulle** in reported speech: *"Du ska klara det"* → *Jag sa att du skulle klara det.* **Vad sa jag?** is the Swedish "What did I tell you?" / "Told you so".

**påstod tydligen** — **tydligen** (**TÜD-lee-en**) means "apparently" and signals second-hand information. It's the natural word when you pass on something you heard: *Det ska tydligen regna i morgon.*

**Det berättar vi inte för Mattias** — *berätta* means "to tell" (a story, news) and takes **för** before the person: *berätta **för** någon*. *Berätta mig* is wrong. *Säga* also uses a preposition: *säga **till** någon* — but most often Swedes simply leave the person out.

**hon bad mig att säga till** — English "ask" has two jobs, Swedish has two verbs. **Fråga** is asking a question (*hon frågade om jag ville stanna*); **be** (*ber – bad – har bett*) is asking someone to do something (*hon bad mig att säga till*). *Bad* is pronounced **bahd**, exactly like *bad* (bath).

**Jag sa att jag inte visste än** — a reported statement with tense shift (*vet → visste*) and BIFF (*inte* before *visste*) at the same time. Notice also *menade inte att du skulle flytta*: *mena* (**MEH-nah**) is "to mean, to intend" — *Vad menar du?* (What do you mean?).

grammars.title: Reporting questions and requests
body: **Yes/no questions** are reported with **om** (if, whether). **Question-word questions** keep their question word — and add *som* when it is the subject (Unit 11). **Requests and orders** are reported with **be** (*bad*) + object + *att* + infinitive.

head: Direct
Reported
rows: Hon undrade **vem som** hade skrivit mejlet.
Hon **bad mig att** säga till om jag fastnade.
Hon **bad mig att inte** glömma paraplyet.
Hon **sa åt mig att** ringa henne. (more direct, almost an order)

after: Reported questions use **straight word order** — no inversion: *hon frågade om jag **ville***, not *om ville jag*. This is the most frequent error at this level, because the direct question is still ringing in your ears.
With *be* and *säga åt*, *inte* goes in front of the infinitive: *…att **inte** glömma*. In speech, *att* is often dropped after *bad mig*: *Hon bad mig ringa henne.*

blocks.text: Retelling a conversation with nothing but *sa… sa… sa…* quickly gets dull. Swedish has a set of reporting verbs that also tell the listener **how** something was said. Most are followed by *att* + a clause.

head: Verb (present – past – supine)
English
Example
rows: Kunden **påstod** att de aldrig hade fått mejlet.
Jag **lovade** att ringa. / …att jag skulle ringa.
Han **erkände** att han hade glömt det.

blocks.text: A shortcut for second-hand information is **enligt** (according to): ***Enligt** Karin var kunden nöjd.* Combined with *tydligen*, it lets you pass on news without taking responsibility for it — a very useful skill in any office.

blocks.title: Säga, berätta, tala, prata
items: **säga** — to say (exact words, short content): *Vad sa du?*
**berätta** — to tell (a story, news, what happened): *Berätta om helgen!*
**prata** — to talk, to chat (everyday): *Vi pratade länge.*
**tala** — to speak (more formal; languages, speeches): *Hon talar fyra språk.*

sections.title: Talking about your progress at work

blocks.text: Swedish workplaces take regular one-to-one talks seriously. Employees have an annual **utvecklingssamtal** (development talk) with their manager, and interns usually get a check-in halfway through, a **halvtidssamtal**. The tone is informal and two-way: the manager will also ask what *you* think could be better — and expects an honest answer.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Svenska 102, Unit 15
items: Think of the last conversation you had in any language. Report five things the other person said, using five different verbs from the table above.
Report two questions they asked you: one with *om*, one with a question word.
Report one request with *bad mig att…* — and check that every *inte* is in the right place.

to ask (someone to do something) (ber – bad – bett)
